Maya: Quick q — customer is asking if they can shard BYOK HSM keys across regions for lower latency but keep custody boundaries strict. Any compliance or ops blockers?
Ajay: Short answer: possible, but big caveats. If key material never leaves the customer HSM and we act as a proxy, custody is preserved.
Ajay: Main risks: our proxy metadata/logs, cross-region admin scopes, and rewrap/unwrap APIs that could be abused.
Liam: RBAC problem: currently our key APIs are global. We should add resource-scoped RBAC (eg, key:region or key:tenant:region) so ops in eu-west cannot touch us-east keys.
Liam: Proposed policy snippet:```json
{"effect":"allow","action":["kms:Rewrap","kms:DescribeKey"],"resource":"arn:redwood:kms:eu-west:123:key/*","condition":{"StringEquals":{"redwood:region":"eu-west"}}}
```
Sophia: That looks right. On KMS integration: we only store key IDs/multihashes, never key material. If customer requires attestation (HW attestation), audit should record attest artifacts and timestamped signatures. Retention + integrity guaranteed.
Ajay: For incident response: we need a documented break-glass flow for cross-region failover. Oncall must not be able to export plaintext keys — only trigger an automated rewrap that moves encrypted key blobs between regions with customer consent.
Oncall-ops: We need a short runbook template. Suggest steps: 1) Confirm customer consent + legal signoff, 2) Verify attestation, 3) Trigger controlled rewrap, 4) Validate checksums, 5) Post-incident audit. Example commands:```bash
# trigger rewrap
redwood-cli kms rewrap --key-id K-abc123 --to-region eu-west --reason "failover"
# verify
redwood-cli kms verify --key-id K-abc123 --checksum abcdef
```
Maya: Another question: customers want "non-repudiation" — signing of audit events with a hardware key. Is that practical? That means our audit exporter needs to HSM-sign logs or ship signed digests to customer. Chain-of-custody implications.
Sophia: It's doable but increases scope: we need an HSM key accessible only to the audit subsystem, strict entropy and key rotation rules, and proof of signing. Also retention/WORM required by some banks.
sec-bot: Reminder: Any RBAC change that affects cross-region access must include a short threat model, list of audit events to log, and an audit retention plan. See template: https://redwood.internal/security/rbac-change-template
Sophia: Also flagged: CVE-2025-XXXX in hsm-proxy v1.3.5 (lib parsing edge-case). Upgrade to 1.4.2 before enabling automated cross-region proxying.
Liam: Agreed. Also, do not store long-lived KMS creds in configs for the rewrap agent — use instance roles / short-lived tokens and assume-role with MFA where required.
Ajay: Compliance note: EU banks want 7 years of key provenance + signed audit chain. We'll need archival to WORM storage and an ops cost estimate.
Maya: Action items: (1) Liam — draft RBAC PR with region-scoped resources + tests, (2) Sophia — spike audit-event HSM signing and retention flow, (3) Oncall-ops — write break-glass + runbook template, (4) Ajay — coordinate legal for EU retention SLAs, (5) Security — schedule proxy lib patch canary.
Oncall-ops: +1 I’ll own the runbook and add a step-by-step playbook doc and pager hooks.
Sophia: I’ll take the signing spike. Will post design + threat model by EOW.
Liam: I'll open the RBAC PR and include the test harness.
Maya: Thanks — looping @sec-bot for checklist enforcement. Will sync in async thread if blockers show up.
